This is the model_b side of case config_cross_domain, trial 0. Compare concept-for-concept against the fixture at benchmark/cases/config_cross_domain/model_b*.json.

concepts.label: underlay
concepts.gloss: A service underlay is the controller binding to the lower-layer transport resource over which an IP/VPN service is carried.
concepts.example: Underlay binding U-7 supplies the transport path used to carry service SVC-42 between New York and Frankfurt.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “underlay-binding,” relation “carries-service” to c.service, and instance “U-7 (under SVC-42)”; ruled out c.service because this is the supporting transport binding rather than the customer-facing IP/VPN service.

concepts.label: attachment
concepts.gloss: An attachment is a service-specific endpoint where an IP/VPN service connects to an access site or interface and carries that endpoint’s VLAN encapsulation.
concepts.example: SVC-42 has attachment att-NY-SVC42 in New York, with C-VLAN 100 borne on that attachment.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “attachment-point,” relations “of-service” to c.service and “bears” c.vlan, plus instances “att-NY-SVC42” and “att-FRA-SVC42”; ruled out c.vlan because an attachment is the service endpoint on which encapsulation is configured, not the encapsulation identifier itself.

concepts.label: rate
concepts.gloss: The rate is the committed information rate allocated to a service, expressed as a bandwidth value.
concepts.example: SVC-42 is provisioned with a CIR of 5 Gbit/s.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “rate,” synonym “CIR,” relation “of-service” to c.service, and instance “5 Gbit/s CIR”; ruled out c.grade because this is a quantified committed bandwidth rather than a named service class.

concepts.label: latency
concepts.gloss: Latency is the service’s delay objective, represented by a named tier associated with a maximum permitted latency.
concepts.example: SVC-42 uses latency tier T2, requiring latency no greater than 8 ms.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “latency,” synonym “tier,” relation “of-service” to c.service, and instance “tier T2 (<=8ms)”; ruled out c.grade because the tier denotes a bounded delay objective rather than a general gold/silver/bronze class.

concepts.label: protection
concepts.gloss: Protection is the resilience requirement specifying which transport failures a service must continue operating through.
concepts.example: SVC-42 is configured to remain available after the failure of any one carrying path.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “protection,” relation “of-service” to c.service, and instance “survive one path failure”; ruled out c.underlay because protection states the required failure resilience, not the transport resource carrying the service.

concepts.label: grade
concepts.gloss: A grade is a named service class, such as gold, silver, or bronze, used to select a predefined overall treatment or quality level for a service.
concepts.example: SVC-42 is assigned the gold grade, selecting the controller’s gold-class service treatment.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “service-class,” relation “of-service” to c.service, and ordered-looking instances “gold,” “silver,” and “bronze”; ruled out c.latency because grade is a broad named service class rather than a delay tier with an explicit millisecond bound.

concepts.label: vlan
concepts.gloss: A VLAN is the customer VLAN tag used as the layer-2 encapsulation that identifies service traffic on a particular attachment.
concepts.example: Attachment att-NY-SVC42 identifies SVC-42 traffic using customer VLAN tag C-VLAN 100.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “encapsulation,” synonyms “c-tag” and “encapsulation,” relation “on-attachment” to c.attachment, and instance “C-VLAN 100”; ruled out c.attachment because this is the VLAN tag carried at an endpoint rather than the endpoint itself.

concepts.label: service
concepts.gloss: A service is a provisioned IP/VPN connectivity instance that joins its attachments and is carried over an assigned transport underlay.
concepts.example: SVC-42 provides IP/VPN connectivity between its New York and Frankfurt attachments while riding underlay U-7.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “ip-service,” synonyms “vpn service” and “ip service,” relations “rides” c.underlay and “attaches-at” c.attachment, plus instance “SVC-42 (NY-FRA)”; ruled out c.underlay because this is the provisioned IP/VPN connectivity offering rather than its supporting transport binding.
